m.q: Develop a program to input four numbers and output the smallest.

If current value is smaller, replace minimum.
Print minimum after all four values.

ido.question: Develop a program to input four numbers and output the smallest. Use integers in this example.

steps.title: Store the first number
steps.explanation: Use an actual input as the starting minimum. Zero would give the wrong answer if every input were positive.

steps.title: Repeat for the other three
steps.explanation: The first input is already stored, so only three more are needed.

steps.title: Read the next number
steps.explanation: Store each new input separately so it can be compared with the current minimum.
steps.code:
minimum = int(input("Number?"))
for i = 1 to 3
    number = int(input("Number?"))

steps.title: Compare the values
steps.explanation: Only replace the minimum if the new number is smaller.
steps.code:
minimum = int(input("Number?"))
for i = 1 to 3
    number = int(input("Number?"))
    if number < minimum then

steps.title: Update the minimum
steps.explanation: Save the smaller value so it is used in the next comparison.
steps.code:
minimum = int(input("Number?"))
for i = 1 to 3
    number = int(input("Number?"))
    if number < minimum then
        minimum = number

steps.title: Complete the loop
steps.explanation: Close the IF and FOR so all remaining values are checked.
steps.code:
minimum = int(input("Number?"))
for i = 1 to 3
    number = int(input("Number?"))
    if number < minimum then
        minimum = number
    endif
next i

steps.title: Output and test
steps.explanation: Print after the loop. Inputs 8, 3, 5, 2 give 2; the final minimum is not always the final input.
steps.code:
minimum = int(input("Number?"))
for i = 1 to 3
    number = int(input("Number?"))
    if number < minimum then
        minimum = number
    endif
next i
print(minimum)
